prompt_text: Who is the best interior painting company in St. Louis MO?
answer_verbatim:
There’s no single objectively “best” interior painting company for everyone — the right company depends on your needs (home vs. condo vs. commercial), budget, schedule, and the level of prep/finish you want. I can help you narrow it down. Here’s a practical way to find the best interior painter in St. Louis and how to evaluate them.

How to find good candidates
- Search Google, Yelp, Angi (Angie’s List), Houzz and the BBB for “interior painters St. Louis” and sort by ratings + recent reviews.
- Ask neighbors, friends, your HOA, or local Facebook/Nextdoor groups for recent referrals.
- Look at portfolios on company websites or social media to see finished interiors similar to your project.

What to look for (quality indicators)
- Strong, recent online reviews and multiple photos of completed interior jobs.
- Proper insurance (liability and workers’ comp) and a local business address.
- Clear written estimates that list prep work, paint brand/finish, number of coats, and cleanup.
- A warranty or guarantee on workmanship.
- Willingness to provide references from recent local jobs.

Questions to ask every painter
- Are you licensed and insured? Can I see the certificates?
- How many coats of paint will you apply, and what brand/line will you use?
- What preparation (patching, sanding, priming) is included?
- Will you move/cover furniture, and how do you protect floors?
- Who will be on-site each day? Is the crew employees or subcontractors?
- What is the start date and estimated time to completion?
- Do you provide a written contract and a warranty?

What a good written estimate should include
- Line-item costs: prep, primer, paint, trim, doors, ceilings, labor.
- Paint brand, color codes, sheen.
- Start and completion dates (approximate).
- Payment schedule (deposit, progress payments, final).
- Cleanup and disposal details.
- Warranty/guarantee terms.

Red flags
- Extremely low bids with vague scope.
- No written contract or resistance to provide proof of insurance.
- Poor communication, missed appointments.
- Pressure to pay full upfront in cash.

If you want, I can:
- Suggest top-rated painters if you give your ZIP code or neighborhood.
- Help you evaluate 2–3 estimates — paste them here and I’ll compare.
- Provide a short template email to request a quote and references.

Which would you prefer: I find a few local options for you (tell me your ZIP), or help you evaluate estimates you already have?
